title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Payment Posting and Dishonored Payments
content:
**Cashiering standards, posting — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.**

**The rule.** A payment names the charge it pays and is applied only up to that charge's open balance; a payment without instructions is applied oldest service month first, room and board before fees. The business office accepts the listed payment methods; a single card payment may not exceed the card payment maximum. Payments may come from the resident, the representative, a long-term care insurer under an assignment of benefits, a transfer from the resident's own trust account that the resident authorized, or the security deposit at disposition. A dishonored payment is reversed against the payment entry it came from for the full amount applied, and a returned-payment fee from the operator's fee schedule is charged for it. A payment entry is reversed at most once. Once the resident has had the returned-payment limit of dishonored payments within the rolling lookback months, only certified funds are accepted on any of the resident's agreements.

**Definitions.**
- *Open balance of a charge*: the amount of the room-and-board charge or fee, less the payments and credits that name it, plus any reversed payments that name it, as of the posting date.
- *Amount applied*: the lesser of the payment and the charge's open balance.
- *Dishonored payments counted*: the reversals across all of the resident's agreements within the rolling lookback of calendar months ending on the payment date. Certified funds only are accepted when that count is at least the returned-payment limit.
- *Duplicate guard*: a payment entry that already carries a reversal is not reversed again (checked on the system record before a reversal is posted).

**Effects.** A reversal reinstates the amount on the charge it had paid and brings a returned-payment fee for that dishonored payment. A deposit applied at disposition is posted as a payment from the security deposit.

**Hypothetical case.** A charge has an open balance of 1,800.00 and a payment of 2,000.00 names it: 1,800.00 is applied to that charge.
